findings.title: CLOB pricing bounds bypass via lossy round-trip calculation in validateHandlerOrder
confidence_deductions: Requires specific (but achievable) state: low sqrtPriceX96 for CLOB order (-10)
Bounded non-compounding impact: pricing protection bypass, not direct fund loss (-15)
findings.description: validateHandlerOrder in AMMStandardHook ignores the exact sqrtPriceX96 passed in handlerOrderParams (marked /*unused*/) and instead reconstructs the price from (amountIn, amountOut) via SqrtPriceCalculator.computeRatioX96. The round-trip from sqrtPriceX96 -> calculateFixedInput -> computeRatioX96 is lossy due to double rounding-up in calculateFixedInput. At low prices near MIN_SQRT_RATIO, amountOut rounds to 1, and the reconstructed price diverges by up to 18 billion billion times from the actual order price (confirmed: discrepancy ratio of 1.84e28). This allows CLOB orders at prices far below the token creator's configured minSqrtPriceX96 to pass the pricing bounds check.
findings.impact: Token creators who set pricing bounds via AMMStandardHook cannot enforce those bounds on CLOB orders at low prices. Any CLOB order at MIN_SQRT_RATIO with tokenIn > tokenOut ordering will bypass virtually any minSqrtPriceX96 configuration. The token creator's price floor protection is ineffective for the CLOB handler.
findings.proof_sketch: 1. Token creator sets minSqrtPriceX96=1e25 for their token. 2. Attacker calls openOrder with sqrtPriceX96=MIN_SQRT_RATIO(4.3e9), amountIn=1e18. 3. _enforceTokenHooks calls calculateFixedInput(1e18, MIN_SQRT_RATIO) -> amountOut=1. 4. validateHandlerOrder computes computeRatioX96(1e18, 1)=7.9e37 which is >>1e25. 5. Pricing bounds check passes despite actual price being 18 billion times below minimum.
findings.victim: Token creators who rely on pricing bounds to protect their tokens from being traded at extreme prices in the CLOB
findings.extractable_value: No direct extraction - this bypasses price protection controls rather than extracting funds
attack_sequence: Token creator configures minSqrtPriceX96 via registryUpdatePricingBounds
Attacker calls openOrder with sqrtPriceX96=MIN_SQRT_RATIO (far below min bound)
calculateFixedInput produces amountOut=1 due to double rounding up
Pricing bounds check passes because 7.9e37 > minSqrtPriceX96
Order is placed at a price the token creator explicitly prohibited
prerequisites: Token must have pricing bounds set
Order at low sqrtPriceX96 where calculateFixedInput rounds to small amountOut

findings.title: CLOB insolvency when tokenOut is fee-on-transfer token — no balance check on AMM->CLOB tokenOut transfer
confidence_deductions: Requires specific (but achievable) state: FOT token used as tokenOut in CLOB (-10)
No full integration Forge PoC (analysis-level with math proof) (-10)
findings.description: CLOBTransferHandler.depositToken (line 362-370) explicitly rejects fee-on-transfer tokens via balance check, showing developer awareness of FOT risk. However, when the AMM sends tokenOut to the CLOB during swap settlement (AMMModule.sol:2239), there is NO balance check on the CLOB side. The AMM sends amountOut via safeTransfer, but with FOT tokens the CLOB receives amountOut*(1-feeRate). Meanwhile, fillOrder already credited makers with the full calculated amounts based on amountOut. The CLOB's tokenOut balance is therefore short by amountOut*feeRate, creating first-in-first-out insolvency where early maker withdrawals succeed but later ones fail.
findings.impact: For each fill with FOT tokenOut, CLOB deficit grows by amountOut*feeRate. With 5% FOT and 1000 ETH fill: 50 ETH deficit per fill. Accumulated over multiple fills, later makers cannot withdraw their credited balances.
findings.proof_sketch: 1. CLOB receives amountOut*(1-f) from AMM. 2. fillOrder credits makers with sum(stepOutput). 3. sum(stepOutput) + fillOutputRemaining = amountOut. 4. afterSwapRefund sends fillOutputRemaining to executor. 5. CLOB net balance = amountOut*(1-f) - fillOutputRemaining. 6. Makers owed = sum(stepOutput) = amountOut - fillOutputRemaining. 7. DEFICIT = sum(stepOutput) - (amountOut*(1-f) - fillOutputRemaining) = amountOut*f.
findings.victim: CLOB makers who cannot withdraw their tokenOut balances after FOT-induced insolvency
findings.extractable_value: Last-to-withdraw makers lose up to cumulative amountOut * feeRate across all fills
attack_sequence: FOT token (e.g., USDT-like with fee) is tokenOut in CLOB order book
Multiple makers deposit tokenIn and open CLOB orders
Swap executes through CLOB handler: AMM calls ammHandleTransfer
fillOrder credits all makers with full calculated amountOut
AMM sends amountOut of FOT token to CLOB, but FOT fee reduces actual receipt
CLOB balance is now short by amountOut * feeRate
Early makers withdraw successfully, late makers fail with insufficient balance
prerequisites: Token used as tokenOut must be fee-on-transfer
CLOB handler must be used for the swap

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R8-HH-04: TOCTOU pricing bounds — stale CLOB orders fillable after bounds tightening
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Design behavior — individual CLOB order prices are validated at openOrder time, pool-level pricing validated during fills. Token creators cannot retroactively enforce tighter bounds on existing orders, but this is expected behavior given the CLOB's role as a persistent order book. The alternative (re-validating every order on every bounds change) would be prohibitively expensive.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R8-HH-07: Sentinel bucket orderId=0 collision with storage slot 0 (nextOrderNonce)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Safe by design — when traverseCLOB reaches the sentinel at type(uint160).max, the sentinel bucket's inputAmountRemaining is 0 (never written), so the fillOrder loop exits with InsufficientInputToFill revert if there's remaining input. The Order data at slot 0 is never used for actual fills.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R8-TS-01: Cross-swap transient storage leak in DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Known issue CP-001/CP-004 (already reported as HOOK-001). The slot is written in beforeSwap but never cleared. In multi-swap same-TX scenarios, Swap B can read stale value from Swap A if Swap B has afterSwap but not beforeSwap flag. This is documented in audit memory as a known confirmed pattern.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R8-TS-02: __activateTstore mid-swap residue on pre-cancun chains
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Not applicable on cancun EVM target. The codebase targets cancun (foundry.toml: evm_version=cancun), so tstore is always available. The sstore fallback path and _onTstoreSupportActivated are never used in production.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R8-TS-03: afterSwapRefund reentrancy into CLOB via WNATIVE withdrawal
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Reentrancy window exists but no profitable exploit path. The fill is already complete when afterSwapRefund is called. The executor can re-enter CLOB functions (depositToken, openOrder, closeOrder) via receive() callback, but these operations modify their own state correctly. No double-counting or value extraction found. Each CLOB function is individually protected by nonReentrant.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R8-TS-04: collectHookFeesByHook queue bypass during fee distribution (ERC-777 callback)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: No value extraction possible. During _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers, SWAP_GUARD_FLAG is cleared (line 3190), allowing ERC-777 callback to call collectHookFeesByHook for immediate transfer. But tokensOwed is decremented BEFORE transfer (line 3130-3131), preventing double-spend. The hook can only collect genuinely owed fees.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R8-TS-07: Direct swap pricing bounds DoS when price moves outside bounds
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Design behavior — direct swaps at poolType=address(0) apply bidirectional pricing bounds enforcement (both directions blocked when outside bounds), while pool swaps allow recovery direction. This is intentional: direct swaps don't have a pool state to compare direction against. Token creators who set tight pricing bounds accept temporary direct swap DoS risk. Classified as self-inflicted config per FP patterns.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R8-HH-05: Direct swap slot collision when same AMMStandardHook for both tokens
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Known FP pattern (digest: 'Transient storage slot overwrite — by-design'). Both hook calls receive the same swapAmount (computed once at AMMModule:2368), so the second write is identical to the first. No data corruption.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R8-TS-05: SqrtPriceCalculator precision at extreme ratios causing bounds bypass
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: The precision issue at extreme ratios (amount1/amount0 > 2^192) causes computeRatioX96 to return 0, which is caught by the sqrtPriceX96==0 check (AMMStandardHook.sol:847). For non-zero results, the _sqrt error is small (0 bps at 1:1 ratio). The extreme ratios needed to trigger material error are only reachable via the H-R8-HH-01 rounding issue, which is reported separately.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H-R8-TS-06: calculateFixedInput double rounding accumulation across many fills
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Confirmed but dust-level: maximum extra is 2 wei per fill step. With 1000 minimum-sized orders at an odd price, the accumulated difference was 632 wei (measured). Even with high-decimal tokens, the per-fill excess is bounded by 2 wei * N steps, which is economically negligible. Does not meet submission threshold.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If a maker calls openOrder with sqrtPriceX96=MIN_SQRT_RATIO and orderAmount=1e18, calculateFixedInput rounds amountOut to 1, and computeRatioX96(1e18,1) reconstructs as 7.9e37, passing virtually any reasonable minSqrtPriceX96 bound.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMStandardHook.sol:218 — the guard checks sqrtPriceX96 < bounds.minSqrtPriceX96 but sqrtPriceX96 is reconstructed and massively inflated
hypothesis_results.detail: CONFIRMED. Discrepancy ratio of 1.84e28 demonstrated between actual order price and reconstructed price. Test test_H01_roundtripPricingBypass_atMinSqrtRatio shows amountOut=1 and reconstructed price=7.9e37 for actual price of 4.3e9.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: The handler encodes the exact sqrtPriceX96 into handlerOrderParams (CLOBTransferHandler:591) but validateHandlerOrder marks handlerOrderParams as /*unused*/ (AMMStandardHook:205) and reconstructs from amounts instead.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMStandardHook.sol:205 — handlerOrderParams parameter is declared but ignored
hypothesis_results.detail: CONFIRMED. This is the root cause of H-R8-HH-01. The exact order price is available in calldata but discarded in favor of a lossy reconstruction. Test test_H03_handlerOrderParamsIgnored demonstrates the ignored parameter.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If tokenOut is a FOT token, the AMM sends amountOut to CLOB but CLOB receives amountOut*(1-feeRate). Makers are credited with full calculated amounts. CLOB deficit = amountOut*feeRate per fill.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: CLOBTransferHandler.sol:362-370 — depositToken has balance check for FOT, but NO equivalent check for tokenOut received from AMM fills
hypothesis_results.detail: CONFIRMED as LEAD. Math proof shows deficit = amountOut*feeRate per fill. Test test_H02_fotTokenInsolvencyAnalysis demonstrates 50e18 deficit on 1000e18 fill with 5% FOT. The CLOB explicitly rejects FOT on deposits but not on AMM fill receipts.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: If bounds are tightened after orders are placed, old orders remain fillable at their original prices. This is design behavior — re-validating all orders on bounds change would be prohibitively expensive for an on-chain order book.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: CLOBTransferHandler.sol:534 — _enforceTokenHooks called only at openOrder, not at fill
hypothesis_results.detail: Design behavior. The CLOB is a persistent order book; retroactive bounds enforcement would require iterating all orders. Pool-level pricing still enforced during fills.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: When traverseCLOB reaches sentinel at type(uint160).max, the sentinel bucket's inputAmountRemaining is 0, causing the fill loop to exit cleanly.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: CLOBHelper.sol:220 — orderInputRemaining == 0 check handles the sentinel case
hypothesis_results.detail: The sentinel handling is safe. The Order at storage slot 0 is never used for actual fills because the inputAmountRemaining guard prevents it.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: This is known issue CP-001/CP-004, already reported as HOOK-001 in prior runs. The transient storage leak is a documented pattern.

hypothesis_results.detail: Known confirmed pattern CP-001. Not a new finding.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: The reentrancy window exists but the fill is already complete. The executor can re-enter CLOB functions but each function is individually atomic (nonReentrant protected). No double-counting possible.

hypothesis_results.detail: Reentrancy window exists but no profitable exploit. Each CLOB function is independently protected.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: tokensOwed is decremented BEFORE transfer in _transferHookFeesByHook (line 3130-3131). Even with ERC-777 callback re-entering collectHookFeesByHook, the fee balance is already decremented. No double-spend.

hypothesis_results.refutation_case: Direct swap bidirectional enforcement is intentional. Direct swaps have no pool state to compare direction against. The DoS is temporary (admin can update bounds, or pool swaps can move price back). This matches the 'self-inflicted config' FP pattern.
hypothesis_results.guard_location: AMMStandardHook.sol:858,866 — intentional bidirectional enforcement for direct swaps
hypothesis_results.detail: Design behavior. Token creators choose their pricing bounds and accept the risk of temporary direct swap DoS.
